title: Workbench: Snowflake Cortex Models: Haiku 4.5 invalid request parameters error
description:


title: Provider base URL drops the API version segment
description:
## Summary

Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini providers fail to list models (and the provider looks unconfigured) when the user supplies a base URL that is just the host, with no API version path. For example, pasting `https://api.anthropic.com` instead of `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`.

The issue was discovered via https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13976.

See also https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13958/changes#r3352009074 for a bit more context.

I made some stopgap fixes in Posit Assistant to enable Positron Assistant, but that just allows Posit Assistant to fallback on Positron Assistant + `vscode.lm` for comms with Anthropic, masking the issue in provider bridge.

## What's wrong

The `@ai-sdk/*` providers expect `baseURL` to already include the version segment (`/v1` for OpenAI and Anthropic, `/v1beta` for Gemini) and append only the operation path (`/models`, `/messages`, etc.).

When a user enters the bare host, the model-list fetch builds `/models` instead of `/v1/models`, which 404s. The fetch then falls back to an empty model list, so the provider shows up as broken or unconfigured even though the API key and host are valid.

Related: a blank or whitespace-only base URL was treated as "set" in some paths, producing a malformed URL like `/models` instead of falling back to the default.

title: Single-source provider definition: aggregate registration + metadata + completeness invariant
description:
Tracking issue. Depends on the headless LM service ([positron#13730](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13730)) and the bridge extraction ([assistant#1427](https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/1427)) landing first. Complementary to the positron credential pull-model refactor (separate issue) -- together they remove all hardcoded provider lists in the headless service.

## Problem

Adding a provider requires editing hardcoded provider lists in several places across two independent consumers of `ai-provider-bridge`, hardcoded in different ways, so they drift from the bridge and from each other.

- The **headless LM service** (positron) hardcodes four lists: per-provider registration calls in its shared-process layer, plus `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP`, `PROVIDER_PRIORITY`, and `PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAMES` in its renderer layer.
- The **Posit Assistant chat extension** hardcodes registration inline, but derives availability dynamically from the bridge's `MAPPED_PROVIDER_IDS`.

Because availability and registration are sourced differently, a provider can be advertised but not registered. This already happens: `deepseek` is in `MAPPED_PROVIDER_IDS` (so the chat extension lists it via `DIRECT_PROVIDER_IDS`) but `registerDeepSeekProvider` is not called in the extension's registry setup, so there is no client. The same class of drift means a provider added to the bridge can appear in one consumer and be silently absent in the other.

The bridge exports raw materials (individual `register*Provider` functions, `PROVIDER_IDS`, `PROVIDER_MAP`) but no aggregate registration and no presentation metadata, so every consumer reinvents the list.

## Solution

Make `ai-provider-bridge` the single source of truth so that adding a provider that reuses existing auth is a bridge change plus a version bump.

## Deep modules (with tests)

1. **Aggregate provider registrar** -- `registerAllProviders(registry, logger, config)`, where `config` carries the per-provider hooks that exist today (Posit AI base URL + user agent, Bedrock callbacks, Google Vertex callbacks, `allowedProviders` filter). Ships an external-build variant registering only `positai` (same treatment as the existing `providers-external` entry). Consolidates three implementations that exist today (`@assistant/node`'s `registerAllProviders`, the headless service's individual calls, the chat extension's inline list). *Test:* after calling it, the registry has a client for every expected provider (internal) / only `positai` (external); `allowedProviders` filters correctly.
2. **Provider metadata** -- a renderer-safe export (no Node-only deps, separate build entry point like the existing `types` entry) providing per-provider `displayName` and a default priority order. *Test:* completeness -- every provider id has a display name and a priority position.
3. **Completeness invariant test (in the bridge)** -- asserts every `PROVIDER_ID` has a register function, a metadata entry, and (if mapped) a `PROVIDER_MAP` entry. Replaces the consumer-side sync test, which only fires at dependency-bump time.

## Consumer migration checklist

- [ ] bridge: aggregate `registerAllProviders(config)` + external variant
- [ ] bridge: renderer-safe metadata export (display name + default priority)
- [ ] bridge: completeness invariant test
- [ ] positron: headless shared-process layer uses the aggregate registrar
- [ ] positron: headless renderer sources priority + display names from bridge metadata (prefer a renderer-safe entry-point import; fallback: push metadata over IPC at init)
- [ ] assistant: chat extension uses the aggregate registrar (this structurally fixes the `deepseek` gap)
- [ ] assistant: `@assistant/node`'s `registerAllProviders` delegates to the bridge's, preserving the external-build redirect

## Decisions

- Priority is exported as a **default** the consumer may override (ordering is ultimately consumer policy).
- The bridge provides canonical English display names; Positron may wrap them in `localize()` with the bridge name as default, keeping only genuinely translated overrides locally.

## Out of scope

- Credential resolution / `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP` removal -- the positron credential pull-model issue.
- Auth provider registration in Positron core's `extensions/authentication/` -- irreducible for providers needing new credentials.
- The immediate `deepseek` hotfix in the chat extension -- should be fixed directly, not blocked on this consolidation.

## Notes

Safe to defer behind #13730/#1427 (lists are internal; migration is mechanical deletion/delegation -- no lock-in). The deadline that matters is landing before the next bridge consumer (viz builder, quick actions) copies the hardcoded-list pattern. Highest-leverage piece is the aggregate registrar -- it removes the advertise-but-break class for both consumers in one move.
